sentences: This vast group portrait shows an Amsterdam civic militia company setting off.

Group portraits of the time usually lined everyone up so each face got equal space, but Rembrandt turned the commission into a dramatic moment, the instant the captain gives his order and the company begins to move.
The nickname 'Night Watch' came later, when the varnish darkened over the years; it was originally a daytime scene.
In 1715, when it was moved to the town hall, it was trimmed on all sides to fit the wall.
The glowing girl on the left carries a chicken's claw at her waist, the emblem of this militia.
Even now, conservators restore it inside the museum in full view of visitors.
